RHACS_CLUSTER.description: Optional cluster filter — restricts the RHACS search to alerts and images tied to one Kubernetes / OpenShift cluster by name. Mapped to the RHACS search-query fragment 'Cluster:<name>' sent on /v1/alerts and /v1/images. Leave blank to search across every cluster the API token has access to.

RHACS_NAMESPACE.description: Optional namespace filter — restricts the RHACS search to alerts and images tied to a single Kubernetes / OpenShift namespace. Mapped to the RHACS search-query fragment 'Namespace:<ns>' sent on /v1/alerts and /v1/images. Combine with RHACS_CLUSTER to scope to a single (cluster, namespace) tuple. Leave blank to search across every namespace the API token has access to.

RHACS_MIN_SEVERITY.description: Optional minimum severity floor (LOW_SEVERITY | MEDIUM_SEVERITY | HIGH_SEVERITY | CRITICAL_SEVERITY). Mapped to the RHACS search-query fragment 'Severity:<csv>' for /v1/alerts so the Central server filters the alert listing; image-scan vulnerabilities are floored client-side after Faraday severity normalisation because /v1/images does not accept a per-CVE Severity filter. Bare 'LOW' / 'MEDIUM' / 'HIGH' / 'CRITICAL' shorthand is auto-suffixed. Defaults to LOW_SEVERITY.

name: rhacs
title: Red Hat Advanced Cluster Security (StackRox)
description: Red Hat Advanced Cluster Security for Kubernetes (formerly StackRox) Kubernetes-workload policy-violation + container-image vulnerability REST importer. Pulls findings from a RHACS Central console via the canonical GET /v1/alerts (paginated via pagination.limit + pagination.offset, search-filtered via Cluster:<name>+Namespace:<ns>+Severity:HIGH_SEVERITY,CRITICAL_SEVERITY) + GET /v1/alerts/{id} (per-alert detail with the full policy / deployment / violations payload — the list endpoint returns ListAlert summaries) + GET /v1/images (paginated via pagination.limit + pagination.offset, search-filtered by cluster + namespace) + GET /v1/images/{id} (per-image detail with the full scan.components[].vulns[] tree) endpoints and emits Faraday bulk-create JSON to stdout. Each RHACS deployment bucket (alerts grouped by deployment.clusterName/namespace/name) becomes one Faraday host (synthetic 0.0.0.0 ip because Kubernetes workloads do not surface a single stable ip on the alert payload — the pivot lives in the cluster/namespace/deployment tuple) with hostname = {cluster}/{namespace}/{deployment}; each RHACS image bucket (image.id / image.name.fullName) becomes one Faraday host (synthetic 0.0.0.0 ip because image scans live on container layers, not on IPs) with hostname = {registry}/{repo}:{tag}@{image_id}. Per-bucket findings are attached as Faraday vulnerabilities — one per RHACS alert (alert.id) or one per image-scan CVE + component ({cve}@{component}@{image.fullName}) — with [CNAPP] engine prefix, '{policy} on {cluster/namespace/deployment}' (alerts) or '{cve} in {component}@{version} on {registry}/{repo}:{tag}' (images) in the title; description carries policy / policy_id / categories / lifecycle / cluster / namespace / deployment / kind / state / time / enforcement / violations (alerts) or vuln_id / package / image / severity / state / fixed_by / published / last_modified / scanner_version / score / vector (images). Refs include CWE-* (single + list + list-of-dict shapes with the CWE- prefix collapsed, deduped across finding + policy + image meta), finding.link / url / advisoryUrl / vendor_url, and references / links / external_references URL shapes. CVE list harvested via a strict CVE-\d{4}-\d+ regex from finding.cve / CVE / cveId / cves / aliases (string + list-of-string + list-of-dict shapes) + finding.summary / description / title / name / link (token-scan over free-form strings); deduped case-insensitively. Severity normalised from the RHACS enum (UNSET_SEVERITY / LOW_SEVERITY / MEDIUM_SEVERITY / HIGH_SEVERITY / CRITICAL_SEVERITY) and the more familiar critical/high/medium/low/negligible tokens image-scan vulnerabilities carry from upstream feeds, with CVSS v3 / v2 base-score bucketing as a fallback when only a numeric cvss / score is given (≤0/>10 → info, <4 low, <7 medium, <9 high, ≥9 critical); RHACS_MIN_SEVERITY enforced server-side on /v1/alerts (via the Severity:<csv> search-query fragment) and client-side on /v1/images (the per-CVE severity lives on each vulnerability entry, not on the image — there is no Severity: filter for /v1/images). Status mapped from alert.state — ACTIVE / ATTEMPTED → open, RESOLVED → closed, SNOOZED → risk-accepted; image vulnerability state OBSERVED → open, DEFERRED / FALSE_POSITIVE → risk-accepted. Auth: RHACS Central issues long-lived API tokens via the Platform Configuration -> Integrations -> Authentication Tokens page (or POST /v1/apitokens/generate); the token is sent as Authorization: Bearer <RHACS_TOKEN> on every call — there is no separate login exchange. RHACS_HOST is the Central console URL (https://central.<cluster>.example.com for the canonical OpenShift route, or the central-<namespace>.apps.<cluster> Route created by the RHACS Operator).
